subject: Re: Observability add-on pricing — surge smoothing and dashboard tier split
messages:
From: James Liao <james.liao@acme.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: billing@acme.com
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Observability charges during traffic spikes

Hi Sean / Vanessa,

Quick question on the observability add-on pricing: our app has predictable baseline retention needs but experiences short high-volume spikes (campaigns, end-of-quarter loads). Can Redwood offer a way to "smooth" retention charges during those spikes? We're worried about a single large event creating a large overage charge that'd be hard to reconcile in our monthly billing.

Also, we want to split dashboard access between a small number of editors (8) and many viewers (~120). Is there a way to avoid paying full per-seat pricing for the viewer cohort?

Can you send a proposal with at least two options — conservative (minimal change) and a pilot-friendly approach for 3 months? If it helps, I can have finance loop in a PO once we agree on approach.

Thanks,
James
James Liao
Head of Platform
Acme Corp

Attachments: none

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: James Liao <james.liao@acme.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability charges during traffic spikes

Hi James — thanks for the note. I think there's a pragmatic path that addresses both concerns and keeps the accounting simple for Acme. High level:

1) Elastic retention bands (recommended) — keep your committed baseline retention (e.g., 30 days) and add an elastic band for short-lived traffic surges. The band is metered separately but smoothed with a rolling 7-day average so a one-off spike won't bill you at full peak. We can cap the monthly billed surge at a percentage of committed baseline (e.g., 40%) to provide a soft ceiling.

2) Surge buffer pilot — offer a 3-month pilot with a reduced surge rate (20% discount to list for surge metering) if you commit to a 6-month baseline. Pilot includes monthly reporting and one billing reconciliation meeting.

3) Dashboard tier split — two seat classes: Editors (full seats) and Viewers (light seats). Viewers are priced at a fraction of an Editor seat (we typically model 0.15x Editor). For pilots we can waive viewer fees for the first 30 days and offer a phased ramp (50% price month 2, full price month 3).

I'm attaching a quick matrix with scenarios (baseline sizes, capped surge %, example bill impacts) — this is intentionally illustrative. If you'd like a tighter quote, Vanessa and our pricing team will need your 30/90-day baseline token/ingest numbers (rough buckets are fine).

Next steps I propose:
- Acme shares 30/90-day ingest distribution (CSV or estimate)
- Redwood returns a pilot SOW showing surge smoothing + viewer-waiver terms
- Finance concord and pilot kickoff

I'll loop in Kimberly for the seat pricing/discount cadence and to coordinate billing language in the SOW. Does mid-next-week for a 30-min sync work?

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: obs-pricing-matrix-v3.xlsx (pricing scenarios, illustrative)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: James Liao <james.liao@acme.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Aug 2027 08:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability charges during traffic spikes

Thanks James — looping in Kimberly so we can lock down the viewer seat economics and confirm the accounting language.

Kimberly, quick context: Acme prefers to avoid spike-driven overages. Sean proposed a rolling 7-day smoothing window, capped monthly surge at 40% of baseline billed, and a 3-month pilot with 20% discount on surge rates. They also want viewer seats treated lightly with a 30-day waiver.

Can you confirm whether billing can show "surge buffer" as a separate line item (so Acme's FP&A can track) and whether we can agree to the 30-day viewer waiver for pilot customers? If any of these need legal/billing caveats, flag them and we'll surface them to James.

Sean — I'll prep the pilot SOW once we have the baseline numbers.

— Vanessa
VP, GTM Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: none

From: James Liao <james.liao@acme.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Aug 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability charges during traffic spikes

Sean / Vanessa / Kimberly — appreciate the fast follow. Acme is OK to move forward with the 3-month pilot under the following conditions:

- Pilot scope: surge smoothing with rolling 7-day average and monthly surge cap at 40% of baseline.
- Pilot discount: 20% off surge metering rate for the 3-month pilot.
- Dashboard seats: waive viewer fees month 1; month 2 bill at 50% for viewers; month 3 bill at full viewer rate (phased ramp). Editors billed normally.
- Billing presentation: must show the surge buffer as a separate invoice line and include the raw monthly surge metric for reconciliation.

I've attached a lightly annotated SOW (sow-retention-deltas.pdf) — this is not fully executed but indicates our intent. If Redwood can produce a pilot SOW reflecting the above and a short DocuSign, Acme will sign and route a PO to your billing contact.

One more ask — given we may need contract language around dispute windows (e.g., 30 days to dispute billed surge), can you add a clause to the SOW referencing an invoice dispute window?

If you can get a draft SOW by next Tuesday, we'll aim to start the pilot on Sept 1.

Thanks,
James Liao
Head of Platform, Acme Corp

Attachment: sow-retention-deltas.pdf (annotated)
